skill.name: prompt-template-designer
skill.description: Design reusable prompt templates for recurring AI tasks. Use it to identify repeatable patterns, define parameters, and document quality criteria.
skill.summary: Create reusable AI prompt templates from repeated domain-specific workflows.
skill.author: 92Bilal26

content.value_statement: Repeated AI tasks often drift because useful prompt patterns stay informal. This skill helps users turn proven prompts into reusable templates with parameters and success criteria.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether a prompt pattern has enough recurrence before making a template.
Separates fixed template structure from variable prompt parameters.
Defines parameter types, examples, required fields, and recommended parameter counts.
Provides a reusable template structure with triggers, parameters, prompt body, examples, and common mistakes.
Encourages version history, success metrics, and adoption checks for prompt templates.
limitations: Does not run prompts or measure results automatically.
Works best when users provide examples from repeated successful prompts.
Not intended for one-off questions or simple generic AI requests.
Does not include integrations with prompt registries or analytics tools.

use_cases.title: Standardize Engineering Prompts
use_cases.description: Convert repeated code review, debugging, or commit-message prompts into templates with clear parameters and quality checks.

use_cases.title: Build a Team Prompt Library
use_cases.description: Document when each prompt template should be used, why it works, and how teams should evaluate the output.

use_cases.title: Teach Prompt Pattern Design
use_cases.description: Guide learners from repeated manual prompts to reusable templates that capture constraints, examples, and success criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Check Template Worthiness
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: decide whether a repeated prompt should become a template.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this repeated AI task: [task]. I have used it [number] times. Identify recurring parts, changing parts, decision points, and whether it should become a reusable prompt template.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Parameters
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: turn repeated examples into a parameter list.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these prompt examples: [examples]. Separate the invariant structure from variable fields. Propose 3 to 7 parameters with names, types, examples, and required status.

prompt_templates.title: Draft the Template
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: create a reusable prompt template from an approved pattern.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a reusable prompt template for [workflow]. Include when to use it, required parameters, the prompt body, a filled example, success criteria, and common mistakes.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Template System
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review and evolve an existing template for team use.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this prompt template: [template]. Identify over-parameterization, missing constraints, unclear success criteria, versioning gaps, and adoption risks. Return a revised template plan.

output_examples.input: A developer repeatedly asks for conventional commit messages with ticket IDs, scopes, and business-value explanations.
output_examples.output: The skill would classify this as template-worthy, define parameters for changes, ticket, scope, and type, then add success checks for commit linting and readable intent.

output_examples.input: A trainer has several successful prompts for helping learners debug recurring shell permission issues.
output_examples.output: The skill would extract stable debugging steps, variable error context, file location parameters, and a filled example that learners can reuse.

output_examples.input: A team wants to turn a one-time API research question into a template.
output_examples.output: The skill would reject or defer the template because the pattern has not repeated enough and lacks clear reuse value.

best_practices: Wait until a prompt pattern has been used at least twice before templating it.
Keep parameters specific, typed, and limited to the fields that truly change.
Include success criteria, a filled example, and common mistakes with every template.
anti_patterns: Creating templates for one-time questions before a real pattern exists.
Adding too many parameters until the template is harder to use than a direct prompt.
Publishing templates without examples, trigger conditions, or measurable quality checks.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when a prompt pattern has repeated and includes enough decisions to benefit from a reusable structure.

faq.question: Can it create prompts for any domain?
faq.answer: Yes, but it works best when you provide domain rules, examples, constraints, and quality standards.

faq.question: Does it execute generated templates?
faq.answer: No. It helps design and document templates, but it does not run prompts or validate results automatically.

faq.question: How many parameters should a template have?
faq.answer: The skill recommends three to seven well-defined parameters. More parameters may mean the workflow should be split.

faq.question: Can this help with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports reusable prompt design for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when the workflow is recurring.

faq.question: What should every template include?
faq.answer: Each template should include trigger conditions, parameters, the prompt body, a filled example, success criteria, and common mistakes.
